verdict.rationale: Jitsu documents delivery of raw events to the user's own Snowflake, BigQuery, ClickHouse, Redshift, Postgres, S3 and GCS, streamed or micro-batched. Profile Builder writes customer profile records into the user's warehouse, and a community user confirms collecting data into BigQuery. However, user control over the delivery schedule is only implied by 'optional batching'; the micro-batch mode is chosen 'depending on what the destination prefers', and no configurable load cadence is documented. Missing for 10: documented user-configurable batch schedule or frequency for warehouse/lake loads, and independent corroboration of S3/Snowflake profile delivery.

support.subject: As a data engineer, raw events and profiles land in my own warehouse or lake (Snowflake, BigQuery, ClickHouse, S3) on a schedule I control

citations.quote: Delivery to destinations — ClickHouse, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Postgres, S3, GCS, and dozens of SaaS tools, streamed or micro-batched depending on what the destination prefers.
Sub-second speed of data delivery to your warehouse. Optional batching is also supported
Profiles are customer records stored in your warehouse, based on the events data you send to Jitsu.
in ClickHouse, which Jitsu Cloud provisions for you, or in your own BigQuery, Snowflake or Redshift.
It was very easy and straightforward to get started, deploy and start collecting things (into BigQuery).
